item.title: Korosaya to champion opportunities for youths
item.description: Sala Korosaya, a 23-year-old final-year University of the South Pacific (USP) law student, has joined the FMF Hibiscus Festival to advocate for greater opportunities for young Fijians, particularly those without strong support systems. Pursuing a double degree in Law and Commerce, majoring in Economics, Ms Korosaya is also president of the USP Law Students Association.
item.content:encoded:
Sala Korosaya, a 23-year-old final-year University of the South Pacific (USP) law student, has joined the FMF Hibiscus Festival to advocate for greater opportunities for young Fijians, particularly those without strong support systems.

Pursuing a double degree in Law and Commerce, majoring in Economics, Ms Korosaya is also president of the USP Law Students Association.

Through her leadership role, she says she has seen young people appear in court without adequate support to address the underlying issues contributing to their involvement with the justice system.

Ms Korosaya believes many young people struggle to turn their dreams into reality because they lack opportunities, positive role models, and supportive communities.

This, she says, can contribute to some becoming involved in criminal activities.

And she sees the Hibiscus Festival as an important platform to raise awareness about these challenges and promote pathways that empower young people to succeed.

She also believes the pageant’s history of developing women leaders in Fiji’s civil and public sectors strengthens its potential to advance her advocacy.

Ms Korosaya credits her parents for teaching her ambition, hard work, and leadership.

While leadership can attract doubt and criticism, she says integrity has helped keep her grounded.

item.title: Military vows lasting reform
item.description: THE Republic of Fiji Military Forces has vowed that its transformation into a professional and democratic institution is permanent. At the passing-out parade for 145 new recruits at the Force Training Group in Nasinu yesterday, RFMF Commander Major General Ro Jone Kalouniwai told the recruits that the military’s strength was now measured by its integrity and commitment to serving the Fijian people
item.content:encoded:
THE Republic of Fiji Military Forces has vowed that its transformation into a professional and democratic institution is permanent.

At the passing-out parade for 145 new recruits at the Force Training Group in Nasinu yesterday, RFMF Commander Major General Ro Jone Kalouniwai told the recruits that the military’s strength was now measured by its integrity and commitment to serving the Fijian people.

He said the RFMF had deliberately chosen a new character after decades in which the military had been associated with political intervention.

“In the December 2022 General Election, the RFMF ordered every soldier to honour the democratic process, whatever the outcome,” he said. “That instruction broke three decades in which the shadow of the barracks fell over the ballot box. It is now the standard you inherit.”

He acknowledged the November 2, 2000 mutiny, saying the RFMF had confronted its darkest day rather than burying it. He said reconciliation was not weakness but represented a permanent change of course.

Ro Jone said the RFMF had strengthened its operational capability, including deploying a platoon to RIMPAC for the first time this year to work alongside US Marines and the Indonesian Marine Corps.

item.title: Group raises $50,000
item.description: THE Motibhai Group raised $50,000 for the Fiji Cancer Society through the Bushells Fiji’s Biggest Morning Tea at the Motibhai Business Park in Nadi on August 12. Established in 2006, Bushells Fiji’s Biggest Morning Tea is the Fiji Cancer Society’s longest running and largest fundraising initiative.
item.content:encoded:
THE Motibhai Group raised $50,000 for the Fiji Cancer Society through the Bushells Fiji’s Biggest Morning Tea at the Motibhai Business Park in Nadi on August 12.

Established in 2006, Bushells Fiji’s Biggest Morning Tea is the Fiji Cancer Society’s longest running and largest fundraising initiative.

The annual campaign reflects the longstanding partnership between the Motibhai Group and Fiji Cancer Society.

Funds raised will support the Society’s patient-assistance, awareness, and advocacy initiatives, helping patients and their families manage physical, emotional, and financial challenges.

Motibhai Group of companies business development manager — wines and spirits, Nitesh Chand said the occasion demonstrated the impact communities could achieve when united behind a shared cause.

“Cancer does not discriminate. It touches all of us,our mothers and fathers, our brothers and sisters, our friends, and neighbours,”he said.

“Events like this remind us that, in the face of hardship, we are never alone. We are stronger together.”

Mr Chand acknowledged the Fiji Cancer Society’s continued contribution to supporting individuals and families affected by cancer, while advancing public awareness, education, prevention, and early detection.

The Motibhai Group extended its appreciation to participating organisations, donors, volunteers, employees, and supporters whose contributions made the fundraising event a success.

item.title: Report null and void
item.description: The controversial Commission of Inquiry (COI) report into the appointment of Barbara Malimali as Commissioner of the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption was thrown out by the High Court yesterday. Justice Dane Tuiqereqere ruled that the COI was not legally effective after January 31, 2025, because the President had no legal power to extend its term. He said in any event the COI had deni
item.content:encoded:
The controversial Commission of Inquiry (COI) report into the appointment of Barbara Malimali as Commissioner of the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption was thrown out by the High Court yesterday.

Justice Dane Tuiqereqere ruled that the COI was not legally effective after January 31, 2025, because the President had no legal power to extend its term. He said in any event the COI had denied natural justice to the four applicants, including Ms Malimali and former Attorney-General Graham Leung, in not first giving them notice of its critical findings against them and giving them a chance to respond.

Ms Malimali, Mr Leung and two senior lawyers – Law Society president Wylie Clarke and his predecessor, Laurel Vaurasi – issued proceedings last year challenging the findings against them in the COI Report and the actions of the President and Prime Minister in allowing the report to be published.

Justice Tuiqereqere also ruled that both President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu and Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka had failed to give the four applicants procedural fairness by releasing the COI Report to the public before giving them proper notice of the adverse findings against them.

In his 154 page judgment he described a number of the COI report’s findings as “irrational” and blasted Commissioner David Ashton-Lewis’s language in places as “extreme and intemperate”, agreeing with one lawyer that “it was not the language of a dispassionate finder of facts.”

Justice Tuiqereqere noted there was “more than ample evidence” of apparent bias on the part of Justice Ashton-Lewis, concluding that a fair-minded observer would apprehend that the Commissioner approached the inquiry “with a preconceived belief that interference had occurred in Ms Malimali’s appointment”.

He rejected the report’s criticism of Mr Clarke and Ms Vaurasi for visiting FICAC on September 5, 2024, to resolve Ms Malimali’s arrest by her deputy, Frances Pulewai, saying this was beyond the COI’s terms of reference.

He described as “irrational” the COI Report’s attack on the Fiji Law Society for raising questions about the appointment of New Zealand lawyer Janet Mason as counsel assisting the COI. The Law Society had raised with the COI the fact that Ms Mason was facing disciplinary proceedings in New Zealand.

While the judge acknowledged that the COI served a useful purpose and made valid observations — noting his view that it was inappropriate for Ms Malimali to be appointed while an active criminal investigation against her was pending — the procedural and legal flaws rendered the report invalid.

He declared the COI’s term extension ineffective, quashed the adverse findings as irrational or outside the terms of reference, and ruled the report null and void.

The case is not yet over, with the court requiring the parties to appear again on August 25 for argument on whether damages should be paid to the applicants and on legal costs.

Mr Leung welcomed the ruling, noting that the COI had been voided and its findings quashed.

“The State can appeal the judgment, so I think I should be circumspect in what I should say, but I just want to take this opportunity of thanking God for his faithfulness and mercy,” Mr Leung said.

Lawyer Samuela Savu, representing Ms Malimali, said his client was relieved that justice had been served

“It’s been a long battle for Ms Malimali trying to clear her name,” he said.

In a joint statement, Mr Clarke and Ms Vaurasi said the judgment delivered a clear message that governments and commissions of inquiry must act lawfully, fairly, and within their authority.

“This litigation would not have been necessary had the Commission done its job properly,” they said.

item.title: Security measures questioned
item.description: THE Palestinian solidarity movement is calling for greater transparency over the security arrangements surrounding the Israeli Embassy. Fiji Women’s Crisis Centre coordinator Shamima Ali, representing the movement, questioned what specific threat had prompted the heightened police presence around the embassy after police confirmed the additional security was provided at the request of the embassy.
item.content:encoded:
THE Palestinian solidarity movement is calling for greater transparency over the security arrangements surrounding the Israeli Embassy.

Fiji Women’s Crisis Centre coordinator Shamima Ali, representing the movement, questioned what specific threat had prompted the heightened police presence around the embassy after police confirmed the additional security was provided at the request of the embassy.

Ms Ali said the public had a right to know why additional security measures had been put in place.

“The security arrangements currently in place are unprecedented,” Ms Ali said.

“We believe these resources would be better directed toward serving the needs of Fijians, particularly at a time when many communities continue to express concerns about delays and inadequate responses from the police.

“We call on the Police Commissioner and the Government to explain the necessity of these extraordinary measures.”

She said the Palestinian solidarity movement had also encountered heightened police monitoring during its peaceful gatherings and demonstrations.

“We also strongly reject any suggestion that members of the Palestinian solidarity movement pose a threat to public safety.

“As Fijians, we also have a right to know what specific threat has been identified against the embassy.”

item.title: $20m expansion
item.description: DULUX Paints Fiji, the manufacturers and distributors of paint products in Fiji and the Pacific, will be investing between $20-$25 million in a new manufacturing and production plant in Lami. The investment – fully funded by the company – will cover the acquisition of land, the demolition of current structures and the construction of the new facility.
item.content:encoded:
DULUX Paints Fiji, the manufacturers and distributors of paint products in Fiji and the Pacific, will be investing between $20-$25 million in a new manufacturing and production plant in Lami.

The investment – fully funded by the company – will cover the acquisition of land, the demolition of current structures and the construction of the new facility.

In an interview with this newspaper, Dulux Paints Fiji chief executive officer Roshan Singh said this plan was now progressing, and they had identified and acquired six different lots next to the current property at Nukuwatu.

“We are required to expand because our volumes are growing, the demand is growing, our product range is also growing,” Mr Singh said.

“So to meet the demand from our Fiji and Pacific markets, we need to have this investment.

“The current factory that was invested by our shareholders and directors 40 years ago, that took us this far. We want to invest into a facility that will take us 20 years forward, that will be able to meet the demands coming 20 years ahead.”

Mr Singh said the new facility will cater for manufacturing and production.

He said they planned to launch the new factory in the next two years.

“Our target is mid of 2028 and that’s what we’re working towards.”

Mr Singh said the multi-million dollar facility would be semi-automated, with the focus of introducing technology that reduced the human impact in the production.

“But the main focus of this factory is increasing our volume, increasing our production capacity and the main thing is making sure we are environmentally sustainable.

“We are looking at renewable energy and we are also looking at wastewater recycling.”

Mr Singh said they were also expecting challenges along the way and they had a team ready to counter those.

He said this new investment would mean customers in Fiji and the Pacific would have a world-class product that was manufactured in volumes and would be price competitive as well.

Dulux Paints sells 70 per cent of its products in country and the other 30 per cent is sold to the export markets.

It exports to Samoa, Tonga, Vanuatu, Kiribati, Nauru and Wallis and Futuna.

item.title: BAT’s green push
item.description: THE British American Tobacco (BAT) company in Fiji is expected to save 60 per cent off its electricity bills after the installation of new solar energy systems to power its Nabua and Nadi facilities. BAT Fiji general manager James Goldring said the newly commissioned solar systems had cost an estimated $1.5million; and had a combined installed capacity of 806-kilowatt peak.
item.content:encoded:
THE British American Tobacco (BAT) company in Fiji is expected to save 60 per cent off its electricity bills after the installation of new solar energy systems to power its Nabua and Nadi facilities.

BAT Fiji general manager James Goldring said the newly commissioned solar systems had cost an estimated $1.5million; and had a combined installed capacity of 806-kilowatt peak.

“The system here at Nabua has an installed capacity of 660-kilowatt peak, while our system in Nadi has a capacity of 146 kilowatt peak,” Mr Goldring said.

He said the two systems were expected to generate 880 kilowatt hours of renewable solar energy annually and supply 60 per cent of BAT Fiji’s total electricity requirements.

“At the Nabua site, the solar installation is projected to reduce BAT Fiji’s carbon emissions by 32 per cent.

“By investing in renewable energy and energy efficiency, BAT Fiji is not only reducing our operational emissions but also helping to manage our reliance on the grid, particularly during peak times.”

Mr Goldring said the project was also contributing towards BAT Fiji’s sustainability targets of achieving 50 per cent renewable energy usage and reducing carbon emissions by 50 per cent by 2030, compared with 2020 levels.

“This installation forms part of BAT’s broader sustainability program aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions, managing climate-related risks and improving the use of energy and natural resources.”

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said the systems were expected to provide a significant share of BAT Fiji’s electricity requirements while substantially reducing emissions from its operations.

Mr Rabuka congratulated BAT Fiji for the investment and said the Government supported the continued operation and expansion of renewable energy initiatives.

item.title: Hardware firm doubles up
item.description: Hardware company Kasabias Pte Ltd has opened its second shop in the northern town of Labasa. Kasabias Pte Ltd national manager retail, marketing, information technology and customer service Nitinesh Chandra said the company had invested more than $1million into the establishment of the new outlet.
item.content:encoded:
Hardware company Kasabias Pte Ltd has opened its second shop in the northern town of Labasa.

Kasabias Pte Ltd national manager retail, marketing, information technology and customer service Nitinesh Chandra said the company had invested more than $1million into the establishment of the new outlet.

“This investment reflects on our ongoing commitment to the Northern Division, and includes infrastructure development, inventory expansion, operational resources, and staffing to better serve our growing customer base in the north,” Mr Chandra said in a statement.

“We invite everyone – from homeowners and DIY customers to builders, contractors and businesses to visit us, meet our team and allow us to be part of your next project,” he said.

The hardware shop’s new outlet is located on the main Naseakula Rd.

Tui Labasa Ratu Jone Qomate and company chairman Kasmukh Patel officiated at the opening on Thursday.
